🧠The idea, animated

A long sequence splits into a distant prefix (the KV we want to throw away) and a recent window. Watch the distant cache get evicted, a hypernetwork turn it into a weight delta, and the loss snap back to the full-cache teacher:

Frozen encode → Perceiver hypernetwork (learnable queries cross-attend the distant states) → rank-16 LoRA on q_proj+v_proj every layer → score the recent window with the distant KV gone, distilled to the full-KV teacher. Roots: Doc-to-LoRA / Generative Adapter, context distillation (Snell 2022), Fast-Weight Programmers (KV ≈ a weight matrix).

📉Does it work? (yes)

Evicting distant KV hurts — up to ~0.77 nats (2.15× perplexity) at 3% cache.

On trained sequences the hypernet recovers teacher-level loss from weights alone — 97% of the gap.

📈Generalization grows with data

With few docs the hypernet memorizes (held-out < 0). Feed it more documents and a general "fold-the-context" operator emerges — held-out climbs to 85% on unseen sequences at 128 docs.

A training-free closed-form fast-weight (KV ≈ weights, literally) generalizes but recovers only 4% — softmax selectivity matters, so the learned ΔW earns its keep.

🎚️Play: cheap test-time gradient kills OOD

Off-distribution, the one-shot prediction misfires. But the distant KV is there once at adaptation time — so take a few cheap gradient steps on ΔW against the sequence's own full-KV output. Drag the steps and watch held-out recovery climb:

Meta-train the init as a launch point. The one-shot hypernet is a good answer but a so-so starting point. Training it through the inner steps (first-order MAML) makes it dominate at every budget — e.g. 92% vs 82% at 16 steps.

cf. Reptile (2018), learned-init-for-test-time-optimization (Tancik 2021).

🔬Style or facts? It's the facts.

It transfers content, not just style

Split held-out tokens by how much eviction hurt them. The hypernet recovers 92% of the loss on the high-cost tokens — exactly the ones that needed the distant context.

corr( needed-distant , recovered ) = 0.96

A worry: maybe it just smooths local style. So we measured where the recovery lands. It lands on the distant-dependent (fact-like) tokens — and tracks "how much the distant cache mattered" almost perfectly.

Robustness (WikiText-103): the mechanism transfers (per-seq compression ~90%, eviction even costlier at 3× PPL), but amortized generalization needs structurally consistent documents — it shows up on LongBench's same-type docs and not on heterogeneous encyclopedia articles. A clean, honest boundary (and exactly what meta-learning theory predicts).
